title: 26 Live Progress Tracking for Medical Requests Statistics

Critical data compiled from extensive research on medical record retrieval transformation and healthcare analytics performance

-


**Request volume surges strain manual systems beyond capacity -** Payer medical information requests[increased 36%](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) between 2021 and 2022, while Massachusetts General Hospital experienced[44% volume growth](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) over four years, overwhelming traditional ROI departments


-


**Live tracking systems deliver transformational speed improvements -** Leading providers achieve[10-15 day turnaround times](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) versus industry standards of 30-90 days, representing 6x faster service through real-time monitoring and automated follow-up capabilities


-


**Digital automation doubles processing productivity -** Electronic submission systems increased monthly request capacity from[278 to 570 requests](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) , a 105% productivity improvement, demonstrating how live tracking enables staff to handle exponentially higher volumes


-


**AI integration accelerates across legal operations -**[82% of legal teams](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) were considering or implementing AI for e-discovery in 2023, with AI capable of handling[44% of legal activities](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) according to Goldman Sachs analysis


-


**Data quality directly impacts case outcomes and costs -**[77.8% of amendment requests](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) address factually incorrect information in medical records, highlighting how live tracking systems with verification capabilities prevent costly errors affecting litigation and patient care


-


**For legal teams, Codes Health retrieves complete medical records in 10–12 days** on a flat fee basis, while same-day competitors typically deliver only partial records and require heavy client involvement—driving frustration, rework, and client churn.


-


**Codes Health’s domain-specific AI accurately analyzes medical records** for legal use cases and catches incomplete authorizations before submission, unlike general-purpose AI tools (such as ChatGPT) that are not built to reliably interpret clinical documentation.


## **Understanding Live Progress Tracking in Medical Record Retrieval**


### **1. Legal technology market demonstrates parallel growth at \\$31.59 billion**


The broader[legal technology market](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) reached \\$31.59 billion in 2024, providing context for medical record retrieval's position within legal operations infrastructure. This market encompasses e-discovery, case management, contract analysis, and litigation support technologies that increasingly rely on accurate, timely medical documentation. Legal practices implementing integrated platforms that combine record retrieval with case chronologies and insights extraction achieve superior case outcomes compared to fragmented technology approaches.


## **How Progress Tracking Software Revolutionizes Medical Request Efficiency**


### **2. Payer medical information requests surged 36% between 2021-2022**


Healthcare organizations experienced a[36% increase](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) in payer medical information requests between 2021 and 2022, creating unprecedented strain on traditional release of information departments operating manual workflows. This volume surge overwhelms fax-based processes and staff-intensive tracking systems that lack automation capabilities. Organizations implementing platforms with real-time status updates and automated provider follow-ups maintain service levels despite exponential request growth that would otherwise require proportional staffing increases.


### **3. Massachusetts General Hospital request volume grew 44% over four years**


Research documented at Massachusetts General Hospital revealed[44% volume growth](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) in medical record requests between 2006 and 2010, demonstrating sustained upward trajectory predating recent acceleration. This long-term trend indicates structural demand increases rather than temporary spikes, requiring permanent infrastructure improvements through technology adoption. Healthcare systems and legal practices must implement scalable platforms capable of handling continuous volume growth without proportional cost increases.


### **4. Datavant processed over 60 million record requests in 2023**


As network-based retrieval infrastructure matured, Datavant reported processing[more than 60 million](https://www.datavant.com/press-release/datavant-launches-record-request-automation-healthcare-organizations-streamline-health-plan-requests) record requests during 2023 alone. This massive volume demonstrates the scale at which modern platforms operate, replacing millions of individual fax transmissions with digital connectors and automated workflows. Legal practices and healthcare organizations benefit from participating in these established networks through faster turnaround times and reduced administrative overhead compared to manual retrieval approaches.


### **5. Health plans submitted over 15 million requests through digital channels**


Within Datavant's total volume, health plan requests[exceeded 15 million](https://www.datavant.com/press-release/datavant-launches-record-request-automation-healthcare-organizations-streamline-health-plan-requests) in 2023, with the majority now processed digitally rather than through traditional fax methods. This digital transition eliminates hundreds of thousands of manual fax transmissions that previously required individual staff handling and follow-up. Organizations adopting platforms with multiple retrieval pathways—including HIE integrations, TEFCA network access, and EHR connections—achieve superior completion rates and faster turnaround compared to single-channel approaches.


### **6. Digital automation increased productivity from 278 to 570 requests monthly**


Massachusetts General Hospital documented that electronic submission systems[increased monthly capacity](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) from 278 to 570 requests, representing 105% productivity improvement without additional staffing. This productivity doubling demonstrates how live tracking and automation recover staff capacity previously consumed by manual status checks, phone follow-ups, and request resubmissions. Legal practices implementing similar automation through platforms like Codes Health redirect paralegal time toward higher-value case analysis rather than administrative record chasing, while benefiting from a flat fee model and the option for Codes Health to build custom integrations with their CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume customers.


### **7. Leading providers achieve 10-12 day average turnaround times**


Modern medical record retrieval platforms with live progress tracking achieve[10–12 day average turnaround](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) times, representing dramatic improvement over traditional services. For legal teams, Codes Health retrieves complete medical records in 10–12 days on a flat fee basis, rather than promising same-day partial pulls that miss key documents. Competitors offering same-day retrieval typically rely on incomplete data and heavy client involvement, which creates frustration and churn when firms discover missing pages or providers. By contrast, Codes Health’s live tracking, AI error checking, and automated daily follow-ups across multiple retrieval pathways are optimized to deliver complete, court-ready records that accelerate case progression, support earlier settlement opportunities, and reduce case carrying costs for personal injury and mass tort practices.


### **8. Advanced providers demonstrate 15-day turnaround performance**


Record Retrieval Solutions reports achieving[15-day average turnaround](https://www.recordrs.com/blog/experience-faster-reliable-record-retrieval-how-rrs-achieved-our-average-15-day-turnaround-time/) through systematic workflow optimization and real-time tracking capabilities. This performance level requires comprehensive provider databases, proactive error prevention, and persistent follow-up protocols that manual workflows cannot sustain at scale. Legal practices evaluating retrieval partners should compare turnaround commitments against these benchmarks to identify providers capable of supporting aggressive case progression timelines.


### **9. HIPAA establishes 30-day maximum response timeframe**


Federal HIPAA regulations set a[30 calendar day](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) maximum response timeframe for medical record requests, establishing the baseline compliance standard that all providers must meet. However, regulatory maximums do not represent operational targets for competitive practices. Organizations achieving 10-15 day performance through live tracking and automation gain three-week advantages in case progression, enabling earlier medical evaluations, faster demand package preparation, and accelerated settlement negotiations.


## **Leveraging Medical Statistics for Enhanced Decision-Making**


### **10. Electronic Medical Records segment holds major market share**


The[Electronic Medical Records segment](https://www.insightaceanalytic.com/report/medical-records-retrieval-market/3042) dominates the medical records retrieval market in 2024, reflecting healthcare's digital transformation and the advantages of direct EHR access over traditional record reproduction. This segment leadership indicates retrieval platforms with comprehensive HIE integrations, TEFCA network connections, and EHR system access achieve superior performance compared to fax-only services. Legal practices benefit from partners offering multiple digital retrieval pathways that access structured EMR data rather than just scanned document images.


### **11. Insurance companies led medical records retrieval market utilization**


[Insurance companies represented](https://www.insightaceanalytic.com/report/medical-records-retrieval-market/3042) the leading user segment in the medical records retrieval market during 2024, utilizing record access for claims investigation, litigation defense, and subrogation recovery. This segment's dominance reflects the systematic record requirements across property casualty, workers compensation, and healthcare payers. Legal practices serving plaintiff-side personal injury and mass tort cases compete against these well-resourced insurance defense operations that leverage comprehensive record retrieval infrastructure.


### **12. E-discovery dominated legal technology market applications**


The[e-discovery segment](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) led legal technology market adoption in 2024, demonstrating legal industry's comfort with AI-powered document analysis and automated evidence processing. This acceptance creates favorable conditions for adoption of similar AI technologies applied to medical record analysis, case chronology generation, and insights extraction. Platforms combining rapid record retrieval with automated chronologies and breach-of-care identification extend proven e-discovery concepts into medical litigation workflows.


### **13. North America held 36.24% of legal technology market share**


North America captured 36.24% of[global legal technology market](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) share in 2024, reflecting the region's litigation intensity, regulatory complexity, and technology adoption rates. This geographic concentration indicates mature markets for integrated platforms combining medical record retrieval, AI analysis, and case management capabilities. U.S.-based legal practices benefit from TEFCA network access and health information exchange integrations that provide retrieval advantages unavailable in less connected international markets.


## **Real-time Monitoring for Preventing Delays in Medical Requests**


### **14. Datavant network comprises 65% of top 200 US health systems**


Datavant's network infrastructure includes[over 65%](https://www.datavant.com/press-release/datavant-launches-record-request-automation-healthcare-organizations-streamline-health-plan-requests) of top 200 U.S. health systems, providing digital connectivity that eliminates fax transmission for majority of large provider requests. This network density demonstrates the competitive advantage platforms achieve through comprehensive HIE partnerships and EHR integrations. Legal practices utilizing retrieval services with extensive digital connectivity access records faster and more reliably than competitors relying on traditional fax-based approaches.


### **15. Eye Associates reduced processing time from 2-3 weeks to 1 day**


Implementation of automated record request processing enabled Eye Associates of New Mexico to reduce request handling from 2-3 weeks to 1 day, representing a significant[speed improvement](https://www.datavant.com/press-release/datavant-launches-record-request-automation-healthcare-organizations-streamline-health-plan-requests) through digital workflow replacement. This dramatic transformation demonstrates the performance gap between manual and automated approaches when live tracking systems eliminate status uncertainty and manual follow-up requirements. Healthcare organizations achieving similar improvements can redirect administrative staff toward patient care and clinical documentation quality rather than record retrieval administration.


### **16. 77.8% of amendment requests address factually incorrect information**


Research analyzing patient amendment requests found[77.8% targeted factually incorrect](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) information within medical records, highlighting significant baseline data quality issues affecting clinical and legal decision-making. These errors include incorrect diagnoses, wrong medications, inaccurate dates, and attribution of other patients' information. Platforms combining AI-powered insights extraction with human verification identify these inconsistencies during analysis rather than allowing them to compromise case strategies or medical decisions.


### **17. Only 49.7% of patient amendment requests receive clinical approval**


Despite high rates of factually incorrect information, only[49.7% of amendment requests](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) receive clinical approval from reviewing providers. This approval gap indicates many documented errors persist in medical records despite patient identification and formal correction requests. Legal teams utilizing AI analysis platforms benefit from automated flagging of potential data quality issues, enabling strategic consideration of inconsistencies that opposing counsel might exploit or that undermine case valuations.


### **18. Removal requests approved only 27.8% of the time**


When patients request removal of valid information they consider inappropriate for records, providers approve only[27.8% of requests](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) , maintaining most documentation despite patient preferences. This low approval rate demonstrates providers' prioritization of comprehensive medical history preservation over patient comfort concerns. Legal practices must analyze complete records including potentially sensitive information that patients attempted to suppress, requiring platforms with comprehensive retrieval capabilities and missing record identification.


## **The Impact of Live Tracking on Healthcare Analytics and Workflow**


### **19. 86% of patients would enroll in free self-service ROI platforms**


Massachusetts General Hospital research found[86% of patients](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) would enroll in free self-service release of information platforms, indicating massive untapped demand for transparent record access systems. This patient preference supports adoption of platforms offering patient upload portals and self-service authorization workflows that accelerate record collection while reducing administrative burden. Legal practices implementing client-accessible record portals improve engagement and reduce staff time consumed by patient communication.


### **20. 79% of patients prefer electronic record delivery over physical mail**


Patient preference research documented that[79% prefer electronic delivery](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) of medical records over traditional physical mail, aligning with broader digital transformation trends. This preference supports investment in HIPAA-compliant e-signature systems and secure document management platforms that deliver records electronically while maintaining regulatory compliance. Practices offering electronic delivery meet client expectations while reducing physical document handling, storage, and reproduction costs.


### **21. 71% of patients would use self-service ROI for nominal fees**


Research indicates[71% of patients](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) would utilize self-service release of information platforms even with nominal fees attached, demonstrating willingness to pay for convenience and speed. This fee tolerance creates sustainable business models for comprehensive record access platforms. Legal practices benefit from patient-friendly authorization workflows that reduce friction in the record collection process while maintaining professional service standards.


### **22. 65% of patients would generate electronic copies semi-annually**


Patient behavior studies found[65% would generate](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) electronic copies of their medical records semi-annually if platforms made this convenient, indicating potential for proactive record collection supporting mass tort screening and multi-incident representation. Practices serving repeat clients benefit from secure record storage capabilities that enable record reuse across multiple cases without repeated retrieval costs.


### **23. Only 0.2% of patients submit amendment requests despite access rights**


Despite HIPAA rights to request amendments, only[0.2% of patients](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/release-of-information-roi-statistics) actually submit such requests according to University of Michigan Health System data from 2006-2012. This extremely low utilization rate, contrasting with 86% interest in self-service platforms, indicates significant gaps between theoretical access rights and practical utilization. The 430x difference between potential interest and current usage demonstrates massive opportunity for platforms reducing friction in patient record engagement.

Fortune Business Insights reported[82% of legal teams](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) were considering or had implemented AI for e-discovery during 2023, demonstrating rapid technology adoption across legal operations. This high adoption rate for AI-powered document processing creates favorable conditions for medical record analysis platforms utilizing similar technologies. Industry analysis from Lawtech 365 documented that legal technology solutions achieve about[40% time savings](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/legal-technology-market-109527) by streamlining repetitive tasks including document review, research, and administrative workflows. This time recovery enables attorneys and paralegals to focus on strategic case development, client communication, and high-value legal analysis. Medical record retrieval platforms with automated chronologies, missing record identification, and insights extraction deliver similar efficiency gains specifically within pre-litigation workflows that traditionally consume months of case preparation time.
